original_card.question: Can one misleading historical-current claim or missing research cross-reference be corrected?
methods: Trace one confusing path from onboarding to its authoritative source.
Index one tightly related family of obstructions with explicit excluded and open hypotheses.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Produce evidence-backed navigation, preserve historical records and avoid a duplicate global survey.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Repair one confusing path or produce a scoped map of one related obstruction family.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Clear navigation lowers entry cost for central research; a global survey without a concrete fix is not required.
allowed_variations: One historical-current ambiguity or one bounded family index.
scope_change_triggers: Rewriting frozen scientific packages just to change their historical wording.

actual_scope: A bounded index of ten open questions stored in merged packages, each tied to the later merged package whose README answers or partly answers it, with exact question text and quoted evidence pinned to one main commit. It re-verifies no mathematical result.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one navigation repair or one related family index. Frozen packages cannot be edited, so the missing cross-references are collected in one external ledger. It spans seven small question chains rather than one family; each row stands alone.
bottleneck_link: Side result, no bound changes. It supports the overlap step of autoresearch.md: a question stored as open can already be answered by a package that does not cite the asking package by path, so a path-citation or title search can miss the answer.
stop_rule: Stop after the rows whose answering README states the result in its own words. Do not re-verify the cited results, and do not add a row from title similarity alone.
evidence: verify.py checks 10 rows against 30 SHA256-pinned inputs (19 TASK.json, 11 README), requires each stored question to equal its TASK.json entry and each quote to lie inside one README line, and rejects 11 mutated rows, and requires that no answering README cites the asking package by path. Statuses: 5 answered, 2 answered by scope inclusion, 3 partial.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Which other merged packages store an open question that a later merged package already answers?
open_questions.why_it_matters: In all ten rows here no answering README cites the asking package by research path, so a path-citation index and a no-match overlap report both miss the answer. A contributor can spend a session on a closed question.
open_questions.first_step: Take packages whose questions no other package cites by path, search later PR titles and README first lines for the question's named objects, and add a row only when the answering README states the result in its own words.
open_questions.blocked_by: Answers are usually cited by PR number or by object name, so each candidate needs a human reading; an automatic match is only a lead.

open_questions.question: What is the minimum exact fitting rank over all perfect matchings of the P112 plane ports, given a frame packing number of 13 and a known rank-32 matching (row L06)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The cited READMEs give one matching with fitting rank 32 and a floor of 30 that is stated only for the two-support even-group colouring construction. They do not state the minimum over all matchings, and each removed channel lowers the algebraic copy floor of the plane-port decoder.
open_questions.first_step: Read the frame-partition and frame-repair READMEs for exactly which matchings the floor of 30 covers, then test whether any matching outside that construction needs fewer than 32 scalar queries.
open_questions.blocked_by: The floor of 30 is stated for the two-support even-group colouring construction, not for every fitting matrix.

open_questions.question: Does the six-call diagonal-pair floor hold over F4, over F5, and at widths above two (row L09)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The cited audit settles only F3 at width two, and labels its length-five row local SAT evidence.
open_questions.first_step: Run the audit's SAT encoding on F5 after symmetry reduction, as that package proposes, and state which reductions need their own soundness argument.
open_questions.blocked_by: Compute cost, and an F4 implementation needs GF(4) arithmetic.

open_questions.question: Is the general leading constant of N(c)/(c log2 c) above 1/2 (row L10)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The cited README fixes 1/2 only for concatenations of blocks of depth at most two and leaves [1/2, 1] open for the general constant.
open_questions.first_step: Check live PRs and discussions for a depth-three block construction before choosing this question.
open_questions.blocked_by: A constant above 1/2 needs blocks of depth at least three, per the cited README.
